instruction: This environment provides three candidate engineering applications, including BIM-capable applications and a distractor application. Choose an appropriate BIM-capable application yourself. Add Windows to Exterior Wall Shell. Start from the provided init.ifc by opening it in the selected BIM application. The init model is a relevant but incomplete predecessor; clean, complete, rename, subdivide, or add BIM elements as requested instead of replacing it with unrelated geometry. Build or edit the model using real BIM elements such as Walls, Slabs, Zones, Doors, Windows, Roofs, and Stairs where required; use real BIM elements rather than visual-only detail geometry where the task requires model elements. Save the only required deliverable on the Desktop as C:\Users\user\Desktop\result.ifc using the selected BIM application's built-in IFC export or Save As IFC workflow. Export the complete model as IFC4 and include the Zones/Spaces in the export. The init model contains a simple two-room shell with few or no windows. Add at least three real windows to exterior walls while preserving Zones named WORK ROOM and STORE. The exported IFC should contain Zones exported as IfcSpace entries named WORK ROOM, STORE. It should contain at least 1 building storey, at least 2 IfcSpace zones, at least 5 wall-like IfcWall or IfcWallStandardCase elements, at least 1 IfcSlab element, at least 2 IfcDoor elements, at least 3 IfcWindow elements. The shaped model should have an overall size roughly matching X span 10 m, Y span 5 m, and Z span 3 m. The IFC should have unique GlobalId values for IfcRoot objects. Other exact coordinates, room proportions, wall thicknesses, opening positions, materials, library part names, property sets, layers, relationship nesting, and harmless exporter metadata may vary as long as the saved result.ifc satisfies the stated BIM content.
source: Open-choice BIM environment; evaluation checks IFC deliverable semantics rather than the selected tool.
